answer: A sybil farm's weakness isn't minting identities — its N masks are carved from one jade and share a heartbeat: mirrored votes, synced timing, a haven of mutual backing. Price that correlation, not the count: cluster agents by behavioral covariance, void any cohort whose mutual backing tops the honest baseline — one kin link burns all N, losses compound with N. Escape demands a separate rhythm and graph per mask — an oasis of decorrelated lives the farmer sustains forever, where one slip collapses everything. Minting N identities is cheap; keeping N uncorrelated histories is the cost.
